title: The pre-push privacy hook refuses a push adding a secret, says where not what, and never replaces your hook
assertion: After `swerepo hook install`, a real `git push`, run through this checkout's `swerepo`, is refused when its new commits add an AWS access key, a GitHub token, a personal email address or a home-folder path. That holds on an existing branch, on a new branch, and when the secret sits in an earlier commit with clean commits after it. What the push prints, on either stream, names the kind, the commit and `file:line`, and contains neither the matched text nor a piece of it (the user name, the email's domain, the file name in the path, the middle of a key or token). Nothing reaches the remote. Clean pushes go through, the first push of a branch and a later one alike, and the later commit arrives on the remote. `swerepo hook install` never replaces a pre-push hook of the person's own: it exits 1, leaves that hook byte for byte (CRLF line endings) with its mode, and names the full line to add: `swerepo privacy --pre-push --remote "${1:-}"`. A hook that is a link is the person's too, even when it points to text that looks like SWERepo's: the link and what it points to stay as they were.

origin.text: The owner's decision (2026-11-23) and ADR-20261123-24e0: leaks are caught locally before a push, in a pre-push hook because SeamSpec owns the pre-commit hook. Findings name where, never what, as everywhere in the privacy scan (inv_5e3b5ef3, inv_ab57c6ff). Tightened after SeamSpec's reviewer: pieces of the email and path checked too, a clean later push confirmed on the remote, a secret in an earlier commit and on a new branch, and the push pinned to this checkout's swerepo. Marked critical after the hook's review (H55-F04). Final polish at the owner's request: stdout checked too, the person's hook checked byte for byte with its mode and as a link, and the full hint with --remote.
